name: Damour-Solodukhin Wormhole
description: Schwarzschild's metric with a small constant $\lambda^2$ added to $-g_{tt}$, which Thibault Damour and Sergey Solodukhin wrote down in 2007. The horizon becomes the throat of a static wormhole joining two asymptotically flat regions, and for small $\lambda$ an observer needs a time of order $(r_s/c)\ln(1/\lambda^2)$ to tell it from a black hole.
convention: The Schwarzschild radius is $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, and we keep factors of $c$ explicit. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: How would an astronomer know that the dark mass at the centre of the Galaxy has a horizon? The answers on offer in 2007 were that matter falling onto such an object meets no surface, that a newly formed hole would ring at its quasinormal frequencies, and that the theorems forbidding hair fix the geometry around it [damour2007]. Thibault Damour and Sergey Solodukhin tried each answer on what they called "black hole foils", theoretical objects that mimic some aspects of black holes while lacking some of their defining features [damour2007]. The foil they picked was "a very simple type of wormhole spacetime", Schwarzschild's metric with one number added [damour2007].¶The number came from three dimensions and from a worry about unitarity [damour2007, solodukhin2005]. Two years earlier Solodukhin had added a constant $\lambda^2$ to $\sinh^2 y$ in the $g_{tt}$ of the BTZ black hole, which removes the horizon and leaves a wormhole whose perturbations evolve quasiperiodically, as those of a unitary system in a finite volume are expected to, where a black hole's decay exponentially [solodukhin2005]. He preferred a $\lambda$ exponentially small in the entropy of the black hole, an effect of quantum gravity outside perturbation theory [solodukhin2005].¶Damour and Solodukhin made the same change to Schwarzschild's metric: $-g_{tt}$ becomes $1 - r_s/r + \lambda^2$, with $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, and every other component stays as it was [damour2007]. At $\lambda = 0$ it is a black hole of mass $M$, and for any other $\lambda$ the sphere $r = r_s$ is a throat joining two isometric, asymptotically flat regions, with the time Killing vector timelike everywhere [damour2007]. A moment of time is therefore still Ludwig Flamm's paraboloid on both of its sheets, the bridge that Albert Einstein and Nathan Rosen described in 1935 [flamm1916, einstein1935, damour2007]. Robert Fuller and John Wheeler had found in 1962 that Schwarzschild's bridge pinches off before light can cross it, and the wormhole's, being static, stays open [fuller1962, damour2007]. A clock in the throat ticks $\lambda$ times as fast as a distant one, which reminded Damour and Solodukhin of the "frozen star", the old name for a black hole [damour2007]. Schwarzschild's $r$ stops at the throat; four coordinates run through it: the proper radial distance, the isotropic radius, Einstein and Rosen's $u^2 = r - r_s$, and the variable Pablo Bueno and four collaborators used for the tortoise coordinate in 2018 [damour2007, nandi2022, einstein1935, bueno2018].¶Something has to hold the throat open, and Michael Morris and Kip Thorne's condition says what: matter whose radial tension exceeds its energy density [morris1988]. Damour and Solodukhin's metric is a special case of Morris and Thorne's, the one whose shape function is the constant $r_s$ [nandi2022, bronnikov2021, morris1988]. Its matter has no energy density, and they described it as "a high-tension distribution (a kind of brane) localized in a thin shell around the center of the throat" [damour2007]. The stresses, which Naoki Tsukamoto wrote out in 2020, are a radial tension and a tangential pressure, and they violate the weak, null, and strong energy conditions at every radius [tsukamoto2020]. The limit $\lambda \to 0$ is where José Lemos and Oleg Zaslavskii pressed in 2008: the curvature at the throat grows as $1/\lambda^2$, and with it the radial tidal force on a body passing through [lemos2008]. A body of finite size is therefore deformed there however small $\lambda$ is, and "at least in principle, an observer can distinguish between a black hole and an almost singular wormhole" [lemos2008].¶What falls in takes its time coming back [damour2007]. A particle or a light ray needs the coordinate time $\Delta t = (r_s/c)\ln(1/\lambda^2)$, to leading order, to reach the throat from outside, and an observer who watches for less than that cannot tell the wormhole from a hole that keeps what it swallows [damour2007]. For the object of three million solar masses at the Galactic centre, taken to have accreted for six billion years, that means $\lambda \ll \exp(-10^{15})$ [damour2007]. Solodukhin's exponentially small $\lambda$ makes the delay comparable to the time a Schwarzschild black hole takes to evaporate [damour2007].¶The same argument, that an observer with a finite time to look sees only what a black hole would show, covers three more properties [damour2007]. A charge held near the throat produces outside it the field of a charge at the centre, to corrections of order $\lambda^2$, as a charge held near a horizon does [damour2007]. A body falling in sets off the black hole's quasinormal ringing, since for a time $\Delta t$ the signal has met only the potential barrier on the near side [damour2007]. A current fed in at one pole and out at the other meets the surface resistivity of 377 ohms that Damour had found for a horizon in 1978 [damour1978, damour2007]. Hawking radiation, too weak to detect from an astrophysical hole, was left as the one way to tell the two apart on a reasonable time scale [damour2007]. The wormhole also holds something a black hole lacks, about $(\sqrt{27}/4\pi)\ln(1/\lambda)$ long lived waves with $l = 0$ trapped between the potential barriers on the two sides of the throat, a number of the order of the black hole's entropy when $\lambda$ has Solodukhin's value [damour2007].¶After the first detections of gravitational waves, Vitor Cardoso, Edgardo Franzin, and Paolo Pani showed in 2016, with a wormhole cut and glued from Schwarzschild's exterior, that an object with a light ring and no horizon rings first as a black hole does, and that its own modes arrive only after a delay logarithmic in the distance of its throat from the radius of the horizon [cardoso2016prl]. The Damour-Solodukhin wormhole itself got its echoes in 2018, when Bueno, Pablo Cano, Frederik Goelen, Thomas Hertog, and Bert Vercnocke computed its quasinormal frequencies and built the train of echoes from them and from the black hole's first signal [bueno2018]. The echoes follow one another at intervals of $2L/c$, where $L = (4GM/c^2)(\ln(4/\lambda^2) - 1)$ for small $\lambda$ is the length of the throat in the tortoise coordinate, $93.6\,GM/c^2$ for $\lambda^2 = 10^{-10}$ [bueno2018]. Sebastian Völkel and Kostas Kokkotas ran the problem backwards that year and recovered the potential, and $\lambda$ with it, from the spectrum of trapped modes [volkel2018]. Light allows far larger values of $\lambda$ than accretion does: the lensing observables of Sagittarius A* put an upper bound of about $10^{-3}$ on it [nandi2018]. The shadow of Sagittarius A* in the Event Horizon Telescope's image gives $\lambda \lesssim 0.4$ at one standard deviation, and the exponentially small values Damour and Solodukhin had in mind change the size of the shadow by a negligible amount [vagnozzi2023].

related.text: At $\lambda = 0$ the throat is Schwarzschild's horizon and the wormhole is his black hole. For any other $\lambda$ a moment of time is the same Flamm's paraboloid, with a throat that stays open [damour2007].
At $\lambda = 0$ the wormhole written in Einstein and Rosen's $u$ is their neutral bridge of 1935, whose throat is a horizon [einstein1935].

The general static wormhole a traveller could cross, with any redshift function $\Phi$ and shape function $b$. Damour and Solodukhin's is the one with $b = r_s$ and $e^{2\Phi} = 1 - r_s/r + \lambda^2$ [morris1988, nandi2022].

Visser's wormhole cut from Schwarzschild's exterior, the other wormhole made to pass for a black hole. Cardoso, Franzin, and Pani dropped a particle through one with its throat just outside $r_s$ and heard a black hole's ringdown, with the wormhole's own modes arriving late [cardoso2016prl].

Another member of Morris and Thorne's family, with $\Phi = 0$ and $b = \ell^2/r$. Its clocks run at one rate everywhere, where Damour and Solodukhin's slow by the factor $\lambda$ at the throat [ellis1973, bronnikov1973, damour2007].

Simpson and Visser's one parameter change of Schwarzschild's metric, made in the radius, $r \to \sqrt{r^2 + a^2}$. Its wormhole has a throat of radius $a > r_s$, and for smaller $a$ it is a black hole with no singularity [simpson2019].

The black hole of three dimensions, where the change was first made. Solodukhin added $\lambda^2$ to its $g_{tt}$ in 2005, which removes the horizon and leaves a wormhole whose perturbations evolve quasiperiodically [solodukhin2005].

The wormhole of an electric field and two massless Dirac fields, where the electric field carries all of the energy density and the Dirac fields only a radial tension and a tangential pressure [blazquez2021].

coordinates.name: Damour-Solodukhin

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius of the mass parameter, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, the areal radius of the throat
Dimensionless constant, $\lambda > 0$; at $\lambda = 0$ the metric is Schwarzschild's

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$ on either side of the throat, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r$ the areal radius. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $s$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/ds$.
coordinates.kretschmann: K = \dfrac{r_s^2\left(4\left(r - r_s\right)\left(\left(1 + \lambda^2\right)r - r_s\right) - \lambda^2\,r\,r_s\right)^2}{4r^6\left(\left(1 + \lambda^2\right)r - r_s\right)^4} + \dfrac{2r_s^2\left(r - r_s\right)^2}{r^6\left(\left(1 + \lambda^2\right)r - r_s\right)^2} + \dfrac{6r_s^2}{r^6}

coordinates.name: Rescaled Time

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius of the mass parameter, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, the areal radius of the throat
Dimensionless constant, $\lambda > 0$; at $\lambda = 0$ the metric is Schwarzschild's

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$ on either side of the throat, with $r$ the areal radius and $t$ the proper time of a clock at rest far away, $\sqrt{1 + \lambda^2}$ times the time of Damour and Solodukhin's chart. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $s$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/ds$.
coordinates.kretschmann: K = \dfrac{r_s^2\left(4\left(r - r_s\right)\left(\left(1 + \lambda^2\right)r - r_s\right) - \lambda^2\,r\,r_s\right)^2}{4r^6\left(\left(1 + \lambda^2\right)r - r_s\right)^4} + \dfrac{2r_s^2\left(r - r_s\right)^2}{r^6\left(\left(1 + \lambda^2\right)r - r_s\right)^2} + \dfrac{6r_s^2}{r^6}

coordinates.name: Through the Throat

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius of the mass parameter, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, the areal radius of the throat
Dimensionless constant, $\lambda > 0$; at $\lambda = 0$ the metric is Schwarzschild's

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \rho, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ the proper time of a clock at rest far away and $\rho$ dimensionless, changing sign at the throat. The areal radius is $r = r_s\left(2 + \lambda^2(1 + \cosh\rho)\right)/2(1 + \lambda^2)$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $s$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/ds$.

coordinates.name: Isotropic
domains: r \to 0 \;\text{(the far end of the other side)}

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius of the mass parameter, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, the areal radius of the throat
Dimensionless constant, $\lambda > 0$; at $\lambda = 0$ the metric is Schwarzschild's

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r$ the isotropic radius, so the areal radius is $r\left(1 + r_s/4r\right)^2$ and $r \to r_s^2/16r$ exchanges the two sides of the throat. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $s$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/ds$.
coordinates.kretschmann: K = \dfrac{16777216r^6\,r_s^2}{\left(4r + r_s\right)^{12}}\left(\dfrac{4\left(\left(4r - r_s\right)^2\left(\left(4r - r_s\right)^2 + \lambda^2\left(4r + r_s\right)^2\right) - 4\lambda^2\,r\,r_s\left(4r + r_s\right)^2\right)^2}{\left(\left(4r - r_s\right)^2 + \lambda^2\left(4r + r_s\right)^2\right)^4} + \dfrac{2\left(4r - r_s\right)^4}{\left(\left(4r - r_s\right)^2 + \lambda^2\left(4r + r_s\right)^2\right)^2} + 6\right)
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{2048r^4\,r_s\left(4r - r_s\right)}{\left(4r + r_s\right)^7}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{2r_s}{r\left(4r + r_s\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(4r - r_s\right)}{4r + r_s}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(4r - r_s\right)\sin^2\theta}{4r + r_s}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Einstein-Rosen

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius of the mass parameter, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, the areal radius of the throat
Dimensionless constant, $\lambda > 0$; at $\lambda = 0$ the metric is Schwarzschild's

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, u, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $u^2 = r - r_s$, so $u$ is the square root of a length and changes sign at the throat. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $s$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/ds$.
